# Companion Files {#sec-companion-files .unnumbered}

Many tutorials build on a file that an earlier tutorial started. The Excel chapters grow one analysis workbook from Chapter 4 to Chapter 7, the SQL chapters build a script in each chapter, and the Power BI chapters grow one reporting package from Chapter 13 to Chapter 15. If you start a tutorial without that file, download its start file from this page. A start file holds the work as it stands at the end of the previous tutorial, so it also lets you check your own work against it. Each chapter also has a chapter-end file.

## What Each File Contains

Every file states the dataset release it was built from, and it explains itself:

- An Excel workbook has a **Solution Notes** worksheet. It lists the queries, worksheets, and named cells the workbook holds and the steps completed so far. It compares each control total with the value the book expects, and it says what the results mean.
- A SQL script opens with the header comment the SQL chapters use. Each query keeps its two comment lines, and a result line gives the rows it returns.
- A Power BI file has a **Notes** page with the same sections as the Solution Notes worksheet, next to the **Validation** page and the tests the chapters build. Its **Checks** query, in DAX query view, compares each control total with the value the book expects.

The solutions to the exercises, the comprehensive cases, and the capstone cases are public too, on the same release. They are listed at the end of this page.

## Match the Dataset Release

The files are built from dataset release {{< var dataset.version >}}, the release this edition uses (see [Downloads](#sec-downloads)). With a different release, the queries still run, but the values differ from the book and from the expected values in the files.

## Point a File at Your Copy of the Dataset

The Excel and Power BI files read CharlesRiver.xlsx with Power Query from the folder `C:\CharlesRiver`. If you keep your copy of CharlesRiver.xlsx in that folder, a file is ready to refresh. Otherwise, point each file at your own copy once, before you refresh it.

In Excel:

1. Open the file and select **Data > Get Data > Data Source Settings**.
2. Keep **Data sources in current workbook** selected, select the CharlesRiver.xlsx source, and select **Change Source**.
3. Browse to your copy of CharlesRiver.xlsx, select **OK**, and close the dialog.
4. Select **Data > Refresh All**.

The Power BI files come as Power BI projects: a .pbip file and two folders with the same name, which hold the model and the report as text files. A project holds no data until you refresh it, which keeps the download small. In Power BI Desktop:

1. Copy the project (the .pbip file and its two folders) into a folder of your own, and open the .pbip file.
2. Select **Home > Transform data > Data source settings**.
3. Select the CharlesRiver.xlsx source and select **Change Source**.
4. Browse to your copy of CharlesRiver.xlsx, select **OK**, and close the dialog.
5. If a bar reports pending changes, select **Apply changes**. Otherwise, select **Refresh** on the **Home** tab.
6. Select **File > Save as** and save the file as a .pbix file with the name the tutorials use, such as Charles River Reports.pbix. Continue the tutorial in that file.

::: {.callout-warning .watch-out icon=false}
## Watch out

Power BI Desktop's new Power Query experience, a preview feature, has no **Change Source** button. If you turned it on, turn it off in **File > Options and settings > Options > Preview features** while you change the source.
:::

The SQL scripts need no change of source. Make your working copy CharlesRiver_Work.sqlite as Tutorial 9.1 describes, save the script in the same folder, open the copy in DB Browser for SQLite, and open the script from the **Execute SQL** tab with **Open SQL file(s)**. The Part III case uses the view that Tutorial 11.3 saves in the working copy. If you skipped that tutorial, run Setup_Part3_Views.sql once and select **Write Changes**.

## Files by Part

The files for the Excel, SQL, and Power BI chapters are ready.

### Part II: Excel

Chapters 4 to 7 build one workbook, Charles River Furniture Analysis.xlsx, and Chapter 8 starts a second one, AuditAnalytics.xlsx. Each chapter's download holds the workbook at the start of each tutorial that continues it and at the end of the chapter. Point a workbook at your copy of CharlesRiver.xlsx before you refresh it, as described above.

- [Chapter04-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter04-companion.zip): Charles River Furniture Analysis.xlsx at the start of Tutorials 4.2 and 4.3, and at the end of Chapter 4.
- [Chapter05-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter05-companion.zip): the same workbook at the start of Tutorials 5.1, 5.2, and 5.3, and at the end of Chapter 5.
- [Chapter06-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter06-companion.zip): the same workbook at the start of Tutorials 6.1, 6.2, and 6.3, and at the end of Chapter 6.
- [Chapter07-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter07-companion.zip): the same workbook at the start of Tutorials 7.1, 7.2, and 7.3, and at the end of Chapter 7.
- [Chapter08-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter08-companion.zip): AuditAnalytics.xlsx at the start of Tutorials 8.2 and 8.3, and at the end of Chapter 8. Tutorial 8.1 starts the workbook, so it needs only CharlesRiver.xlsx.

### Part III: SQL

Each chapter's download holds its script at the start of each tutorial after the first, and at the end of the chapter. The first tutorial of each chapter starts a new script, so it needs only the working copy.

- [Chapter09-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter09-companion.zip): Chapter09.sql at the start of Tutorials 9.2 and 9.3, and at the end of Chapter 9.
- [Chapter10-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter10-companion.zip): Chapter10.sql at the start of Tutorials 10.2 and 10.3, and at the end of Chapter 10.
- [Chapter11-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter11-companion.zip): Chapter11.sql at the start of Tutorials 11.2 and 11.3, and at the end of Chapter 11, with Setup_Part3_Views.sql.
- [Chapter12-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter12-companion.zip): Audit.sql at the start of Tutorials 12.2 and 12.3, and at the end of Chapter 12.

### Part IV: Power BI

Chapters 13 to 15 build one reporting package, Charles River Reports, and Chapter 16 starts internal audit's own file, Audit Monitoring. Each comes as a Power BI project: open it, point it at your copy of CharlesRiver.xlsx, refresh it, and save it as the .pbix file the tutorials use, as described above.

- [Chapter13-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter13-companion.zip): Charles River Reports at the start of Tutorials 13.2 and 13.3, and at the end of Chapter 13.
- [Chapter14-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter14-companion.zip): the same project at the start of Tutorials 14.1, 14.2, and 14.3, and at the end of Chapter 14.
- [Chapter15-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter15-companion.zip): the same project at the start of Tutorials 15.1, 15.2, and 15.3, and at the end of Chapter 15.
- [Chapter16-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Chapter16-companion.zip): Audit Monitoring at the start of Tutorials 16.2 and 16.3, and at the end of Chapter 16. Tutorial 16.1 starts the file, so it needs only CharlesRiver.xlsx. The folder for Tutorial 16.3 also holds Charles River Reports as it stands at the end of Chapter 15, which that tutorial tests.
- [AppendixA-companion.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/AppendixA-companion.zip): for [the appendix on publishing and security](#sec-appendix-publishing), Charles River Reports and Audit Monitoring at the start of its first tutorial, and Charles River Reports at the start of its second.

## Solutions

Try the work first, then compare it with the solution. Every solution file explains itself, as the files above do: an Excel workbook has a **Solution Notes** worksheet, a Power BI project has a **Notes** page and a **Checks** query in DAX query view, and a SQL script ends with a notes block. Each lists the requirements, the instructor notes, and the values checked against dataset release {{< var dataset.version >}}. The Power BI projects of the capstones read the solution workbook of the same capstone, and the Chapter 19 project reads RefundFlags.csv, from the folder `C:\CharlesRiver` like the other files, so put those files there.

- [Instructor-Notes-2026.zip]({{< var companion.download >}}/Instructor-Notes-2026.zip): the instructor notes, the expected values of the tutorials, and the answer keys of the multiple-choice questions for every chapter, case, and appendix, in the order of the book, as Markdown and Word files
